hypotheses.reasoning: Consumer lag on catalog.updates partition 2 is caused by a single malformed message, msg-595676 at offset 145600, whose body contains a NUL byte at position 1860. index-worker fails to parse it (#3017, #3054, #3350, #3504, #3817). The consumer has no max-retries configured, so it nacks and redelivers the same message indefinitely (#3023 attempt 9, #3055 attempt 14). Partition 2 is blocked behind it, and lag climbs from about 1,000 messages at 19:46:47 (#3285) to over 13,000 at 19:53:17 (#4576). index-worker CPU stays normal because it is retrying rather than doing work. The other errors (status-poller timeouts on legacy-inventory, search-api heap at 80%, web-bff disk at 80%) are unrelated noise. Downstream services show no errors, consistent with the backlog being confined to the index pipeline.

Alternative reading: the NUL byte means the upstream producer wrote corrupt bytes into the catalog record, so the data itself is bad. This is the origin of the bad payload, but the operational failure is a consumer jam, so poison_message is the better fit. The producer-side source of the NUL could not be confirmed from the logs, since catalog-svc logs no errors.
index-worker had a GC pause of 914ms (#2544) and search-api heap is at 80% (#1587), but neither is the origin. The backlog is explained by the single poison message, and CPU is normal per the alert.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or dead-letter msg-595676 (catalog.updates partition 2, offset 145600) so the partition can drain. Configure a max-retry count and a dead-letter queue for index-worker so one malformed message cannot block the partition again. Investigate the producer that wrote a NUL byte into the payload at offset 145600 and add input validation. Once the partition drains, replay or repair the skipped catalog update for that product. Monitor partition 2 lag afterwards.
